newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka assures food supplies to Tamils in north.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka assures food supplies to Tamils in north.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government said on Sunday that attacks on shipping by Tamil Tiger rebels, who last month seized a North Korean merchant vessel, will not deter it from sending food supplies to the north where half a million Tamils live.

The Ministry of Defence said in a statement that the security forces are prepared to deal with any situation if the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels continue to attack civilian and commercial shipping.

The rebels seized the North Korean merchant ship Morang Bong last month eight km (five miles) off Point Pedro on Jaffna, about 300 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo. One Korean sailor died in the hijacking, but the rebels released the 37 surviving crew.

In an earlier incident also in July, the rebels set fire to a refugee ship off the northwestern coast and took away its nine crew. Two Indonesians were later released but the fate of the seven Sri Lankan crew is unknown.
The ministry said the rebels seem determined to deny the basic needs of Tamils who have decided to return to Jaffna peninsula which the military captured from the guerrillas in mid-1996.
Food and other essential supplies are taken to Jaffna by air or sea as the rebels are blocking the land route connecting the peninsula with the rest of the island.

Some 20,000 Sri Lankan troops are battling the Tiger rebels to open a highway through the guerrilla-held Wanni region toward Jaffna. But the offensive launched in May has been slowed by fierce rebel resistance.

"The government will take all necessary security measures to ensure that the supply lines to the Jaffna peninsula are maintained until such time as the main supply route is established," the statement said.
The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for the minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 15th year. The LTTE claim the toll is higher.
